title: Fix SRD class and subclass feature boundary parsing
description:
Problem
The SRD importer still merges adjacent class and subclass features or allows class setup/proficiency prose to bleed into feature records.

Evidence from the 2026-06-07 audit
Affected examples include:
- feature:bard:spellcasting
- feature:cleric:spellcasting
- feature:druid:druidic
- feature:monk:martial-arts
- feature:paladin:divine-sense
- feature:ranger:favored-enemy
- feature:warlock:otherworldly-patron
- feature:wizard:cantrips
- feature:life-domain:bonus-proficiency
- feature:hunter:multiattack
- feature:circle-of-the-land:natural-recovery

Specific failures
- Several feature records include class proficiency blocks such as Weapons, Tools, Saving Throws, and Skills.
- Life Domain Bonus Proficiency swallowed Disciple of Life and Channel Divinity: Preserve Life.
- Hunter Multiattack swallowed Superior Hunter's Defense.
- Circle of the Land Natural Recovery swallowed Circle Spells and table content.
- Circle of the Land appears to be missing later features such as Land's Stride, Nature's Ward, and Nature's Sanctuary.

Required behavior
- Each class/subclass feature record should correspond to one source feature heading or intentionally modeled repeated feature.
- Adjacent feature headings must terminate the previous feature body.
- Class setup/proficiency blocks must not be emitted as feature body content.
- Subclass feature extraction must not silently skip later subclass features.

IMPORTER SAFETY
Importer safety: follow docs/importer-fix-protocol.md. Do not weaken regression tests or audit expectations to match current generated output; fix parser/extractor behavior or document source-backed evidence that the expectation was wrong.
